q: Under the Trade Unions Act, 1926, the name of a registered Trade Union can be changed only with the consent of:

options.A: The Registrar of Trade Unions alone
options.B: A simple majority of the members present at a general meeting
options.C: Not less than two-thirds of the total number of its members
options.D: The executive committee of the union

e: The name of a registered trade union can be changed only with the consent of not less than two-thirds of the total number of its members.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A Works Committee constituted under the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 consists of representatives of the employers and of the workmen engaged in the establishment.
2. In a Works Committee, the number of representatives of the workmen shall not be less than the number of representatives of the employer.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both are correct: a Works Committee consists of representatives of the employer and of the workmen, and the number of workmen's representatives shall not be less than the number of the employer's representatives.

q: Under the Apprentices Act, 1961, a person is qualified to be engaged as an apprentice if he is not less than:

options.A: 12 years of age
options.B: 16 years of age
options.C: 18 years of age
options.D: 14 years of age

e: Under the Apprentices Act, a person is qualified to be engaged as an apprentice if he is not less than 14 years of age and satisfies the prescribed standards of education and physical fitness.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Central Government contributes 1.16 per cent of the wages of an employee to the Employees' Pension Fund.
2. An employee is required to contribute separately to the Employees' Pension Scheme, in addition to his contribution to the Provident Fund.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Statement 1 is correct: the Central Government contributes 1.16 per cent of the wages to the Employees' Pension Fund. Statement 2 is wrong: the employee makes no separate pension contribution; the pension share comes from the employer's contribution. Hence 1 only.

q: The Employees' State Insurance Act, 1948 applies, in the first instance, to factories employing:

options.A: 20 or more persons
options.B: 50 or more persons
options.C: 10 or more persons
options.D: 100 or more persons

e: The Employees' State Insurance Act applies, in the first instance, to factories employing 10 or more persons.

q: The shop on-cost of a shop for a period is Rs 1,35,000. The total direct labour hours booked to jobs in the shop during the period are 9,000. The shop on-cost rate per direct labour hour is:

options.A: Rs 12 per hour
options.B: Rs 15 per hour
options.C: Rs 18 per hour
options.D: Rs 13.50 per hour

e: Shop on-cost rate per direct labour hour = 1,35,000 / 9,000 = Rs 15 per hour.

q: The allowed time for a job is 18 hours and a worker completes it in 12 hours. His hourly rate of wages is Rs 55. Under the Halsey premium bonus plan (bonus at 50 per cent of the value of the time saved), his total earnings for the job (wages for time taken plus bonus) are:

options.A: Rs 825
options.B: Rs 660
options.C: Rs 990
options.D: Rs 720

e: Time saved = 18 - 12 = 6 hours. Time wages = 12 x Rs 55 = Rs 660. Halsey bonus = 50 per cent x 6 x 55 = Rs 165. Total earnings = 660 + 165 = Rs 825.

q: An external screw thread on a bolt or rod is cut by hand in a workshop with the help of a tool called a:

options.A: Tap
options.B: Reamer
options.C: Die
options.D: Broach

e: An external screw thread on a bolt or rod is cut by hand with a die; a tap is used for cutting internal threads.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Under the Contract Labour (Regulation and Abolition) Act, 1970, the certificate of registration for an establishment to which the Act applies is obtained by the contractor engaged in it.
2. A contractor to whom the Act applies is required to obtain a licence from the licensing officer before undertaking contract work.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Statement 1 is wrong: the certificate of registration for the establishment is obtained by the principal employer, not by the contractor. Statement 2 is correct: the contractor must obtain a licence from the licensing officer. Hence 2 only.

q: A machine in a workshop ran for a total of 9,000 hours during a period, during which it suffered 15 breakdowns. The Mean Time Between Failures (MTBF) of the machine is:

options.A: 450 hours
options.B: 500 hours
options.C: 750 hours
options.D: 600 hours

e: MTBF = total running time / number of breakdowns = 9,000 / 15 = 600 hours.

q: Gear teeth are generated in a gear shaping machine by means of:

options.A: A rotating hob
options.B: A reciprocating pinion-shaped cutter
options.C: A formed milling cutter
options.D: A grinding wheel

e: In a gear shaping machine, gear teeth are generated by a reciprocating pinion-shaped cutter; a rotating hob is used in gear hobbing, not shaping.

q: The machine expenses of a machine for a period are Rs 96,000 and the wages of the machine operator for the same period are Rs 24,000. The machine worked for 4,000 hours in the period. The comprehensive machine-hour rate of the machine (including the operator's wages) is:

options.A: Rs 24 per hour
options.B: Rs 27 per hour
options.C: Rs 30 per hour
options.D: Rs 36 per hour

e: Comprehensive machine-hour rate = (machine expenses + operator's wages) / hours worked = (96,000 + 24,000) / 4,000 = Rs 30 per hour.

q: 'Seasoning' of timber in the wood-working shop of a workshop is carried out in order to:

options.A: Reduce the moisture content of the timber so that it does not warp, shrink or crack in service
options.B: Harden the surface of the timber
options.C: Protect the timber against white ants
options.D: Give a smooth finish to the timber

e: Seasoning reduces the moisture content of timber so that it does not warp, shrink or crack in service.

q: Out of the wages payable to an employee, the employer's contribution towards the Employees' Deposit Linked Insurance (EDLI) Scheme is:

options.A: 0.25 per cent
options.B: 1.00 per cent
options.C: 1.16 per cent
options.D: 0.50 per cent

e: Out of the wages payable, the employer's contribution towards the Employees' Deposit Linked Insurance (EDLI) Scheme is 0.50 per cent.

q: The standard cost of material for a workshop job is 500 kg at Rs 32 per kg. The material actually consumed on the job is 520 kg, purchased at Rs 35 per kg. The total material cost variance on the job is:

options.A: Rs 1,560 (Adverse)
options.B: Rs 640 (Adverse)
options.C: Rs 2,200 (Favourable)
options.D: Rs 2,200 (Adverse)

e: Standard material cost = 500 x Rs 32 = Rs 16,000. Actual cost = 520 x Rs 35 = Rs 18,200. Total material cost variance = 16,000 - 18,200 = Rs 2,200 (Adverse).

q: Under the Factories Act, 1948, in respect of lifting machines, chains, ropes and lifting tackle used in a factory, it is required that:

options.A: The safe working load is plainly marked on them and they are not loaded beyond the safe working load, except for the purpose of a test
options.B: They are painted red to distinguish them from other equipment
options.C: They are examined by the occupier personally every week
options.D: They are replaced after every five years of use

e: The safe working load must be plainly marked on lifting machines, chains, ropes and lifting tackle, and they are not to be loaded beyond the safe working load except for the purpose of a test.

q: A turret (capstan) lathe is preferred to an ordinary centre lathe for the batch production of small turned components because:

options.A: It can machine much longer workpieces
options.B: It works at much higher spindle speeds
options.C: A number of tools set in the turret can be brought into operation one after another in sequence, without re-setting for each operation
options.D: It does not require a skilled operator at all

e: On a turret lathe, a number of tools set in the turret can be brought into operation one after another in sequence without re-setting, which suits batch production of small turned components.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Payment of Bonus Act, 1965 applies to every factory and to every other establishment in which twenty or more persons are employed on any day during an accounting year.
2. An establishment to which the Payment of Bonus Act once applies continues to be governed by the Act even if the number of persons employed therein falls below twenty thereafter.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both are correct: the Bonus Act applies to every factory and to establishments in which twenty or more persons are employed, and once it applies to an establishment it continues to apply even if the number employed falls below twenty.

q: The budgeted shop on-cost of a shop for a period is Rs 3,60,000 and the actual shop on-cost incurred in the period is Rs 3,42,000. The on-cost expenditure variance for the period is:

options.A: Rs 18,000 (Favourable)
options.B: Rs 18,000 (Adverse)
options.C: Rs 12,000 (Favourable)
options.D: Rs 36,000 (Adverse)

e: On-cost expenditure variance = budgeted on-cost - actual on-cost = 3,60,000 - 3,42,000 = Rs 18,000 (Favourable), since the actual expenditure is less than the budget.

q: A dial gauge (dial test indicator) is used in a workshop primarily for checking:

options.A: The hardness of a machined surface
options.B: The run-out (eccentricity) and alignment of rotating components such as wheels and shafts
options.C: The pitch of screw threads
options.D: The temperature of bearings

e: A dial gauge (dial test indicator) measures minute displacements, and is used primarily for checking the run-out (eccentricity) and alignment of rotating components such as wheels and shafts.

q: Cast iron, as used for castings in a workshop foundry, is distinguished from steel principally by its carbon content, which is generally:

options.A: Below 0.3 per cent
options.B: Between 0.5 and 1 per cent
options.C: Between 2 and 4 per cent
options.D: Above 6 per cent

e: Cast iron is distinguished from steel principally by its higher carbon content, generally between 2 and 4 per cent, which makes it easy to cast but comparatively brittle.

q: The total cost of a job executed by a workshop for another railway is Rs 2,50,000. Departmental charges are leviable on the job at 12 per cent of the cost. The total amount recoverable from the other railway for the job is:
e: Amount recoverable = total cost + departmental charges at 12 per cent = 2,50,000 x 1.12 = Rs 2,80,000.

q: In flame hardening of a steel component in a workshop:

options.A: The surface of the component is heated rapidly by an oxy-acetylene flame and is then quenched
options.B: The whole component is heated in a furnace and cooled slowly in air
options.C: The component is packed in carbonaceous material and heated for a long period
options.D: Nitrogen is diffused into the surface of the component

e: In flame hardening, the surface of the component is heated rapidly by an oxy-acetylene flame and is then quenched, hardening the surface while the core remains tough.

q: Under the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947, workmen employed in a public utility service cannot resort to a strike without giving a notice of strike to the employer, and they cannot commence the strike within ______ of giving such notice:

options.A: 7 days
options.B: 14 days
options.C: 21 days
options.D: 6 weeks

e: Workmen in a public utility service cannot commence a strike within 14 days of giving the notice of strike to the employer.

q: The standard rate of wages for a workshop job is Rs 50 per hour. The workers actually engaged on the job are paid at Rs 55 per hour and the total hours actually worked on the job are 380. The labour rate variance on the job is:

options.A: Rs 1,500 (Adverse)
options.B: Rs 950 (Adverse)
options.C: Rs 1,900 (Adverse)
options.D: Rs 1,900 (Favourable)

e: Labour rate variance = (standard rate - actual rate) x actual hours = (50 - 55) x 380 = Rs 1,900 (Adverse).

q: 'Counterboring' of a drilled hole in a workshop consists of:

options.A: Enlarging the hole throughout its depth to a bigger diameter
options.B: Cutting internal threads in the hole
options.C: Making a conical enlargement at the mouth of the hole for a countersunk screw head
options.D: Enlarging the upper portion of the hole with a flat bottom, so that the head of a bolt or nut can sit below the surface

e: Counterboring enlarges the upper portion of a drilled hole with a flat bottom, so that the head of a bolt or nut can sit below the surface; a conical enlargement is countersinking.

q: A surface plate is provided in the fitting and inspection sections of a workshop because it:

options.A: Provides a true flat reference surface for marking out work and for inspection
options.B: Is used for sharpening cutting tools
options.C: Serves as an anvil for forging work
options.D: Is used to support workpieces during welding

e: A surface plate provides a true flat reference surface for marking out work and for inspection in the fitting and inspection sections.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Under the Factories Act, 1948, a young person shall not be required or allowed to work on a dangerous machine unless he has been fully instructed as to the dangers arising from it and the precautions to be observed, and is under adequate supervision.
2. Under the Factories Act, 1948, a child worker who is permitted to work in a factory may be employed during the night, between 10 p.m. and 6 a.m., with the permission of the Inspector.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Statement 1 is correct: a young person may work on a dangerous machine only if fully instructed about the dangers and precautions and kept under adequate supervision. Statement 2 is wrong: night employment of a child is barred outright. Hence 1 only.

q: Seam welding is employed in a workshop for making leak-proof joints, such as in tanks and containers, and it consists of:

options.A: A continuous fillet weld made by an arc process
options.B: A series of overlapping spot welds produced by roller (wheel) electrodes
options.C: Joining by heating the parts in a furnace
options.D: Welding with a thermit mixture

e: Seam welding consists of a series of overlapping spot welds produced by roller (wheel) electrodes, and is therefore employed for making leak-proof joints in tanks and containers.

q: During the execution of a workshop job, 25 hours are recorded as idle time of the workers booked on the job. The standard rate of wages is Rs 60 per hour. Treated as a cost variance, the labour idle time variance on the job is:

options.A: Rs 1,200 (Adverse)
options.B: Rs 1,800 (Adverse)
options.C: Rs 2,500 (Adverse)
options.D: Rs 1,500 (Adverse)

e: Labour idle time variance = idle hours x standard rate = 25 x Rs 60 = Rs 1,500 (Adverse), since wages are paid for unproductive time.

q: In the Vickers hardness test carried out on workshop materials, the indenter pressed into the material under a specified load is:

options.A: A hardened steel ball
options.B: A diamond cone
options.C: A square-based diamond pyramid
options.D: A hardened steel cone

e: In the Vickers hardness test, the indenter pressed into the material under a specified load is a square-based diamond pyramid; a steel ball is used in the Brinell test.

q: In the limits and fits system followed in workshop manufacture, the 'tolerance' on a dimension is:

options.A: The difference between the size of the hole and the size of the shaft
options.B: The difference between the maximum and minimum permissible limits of the size
options.C: The intentional difference provided between mating parts for the type of fit
options.D: The deviation of a size from its basic size

e: In the limits and fits system, tolerance is the difference between the maximum and minimum permissible limits of a size, i.e., the permitted variation in the dimension.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Minimum Wages Act, 1948 applies to the employments specified in the Schedule to the Act, known as scheduled employments.
2. Under the Minimum Wages Act, 1948, minimum rates of wages may be fixed by the hour, by the day, by the month or by such other larger wage period as may be prescribed.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both are correct: the Minimum Wages Act applies to the employments specified in the Schedule to the Act, and minimum rates of wages may be fixed by the hour, by the day, by the month or by such other larger wage period as may be prescribed.

q: A ring gauge is used in a workshop for checking:

options.A: The external diameter of cylindrical components such as shafts
options.B: The internal diameter of holes
options.C: The angle of a tapered component
options.D: The flatness of a surface

e: A ring gauge is used for checking the external diameter of cylindrical components such as shafts, on a go and no-go basis; internal diameters are checked with plug gauges.

q: A workshop employee, whose last drawn monthly wages are Rs 33,800, retires after completing 24 years and 7 months of service. Under the Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972, a part of a year in excess of six months is treated as a completed year. The gratuity payable to him, at 15 days' wages for every completed year of service (15/26 of the monthly wages for each year), is:
e: Service of 24 years and 7 months counts as 25 completed years, as a part of a year in excess of six months is treated as a completed year. Gratuity = 33,800 x 15/26 x 25 = Rs 19,500 x 25 = Rs 4,87,500.

q: Eddy current testing, employed for the examination of components in a workshop, is a non-destructive test used for detecting:

options.A: Internal defects deep inside thick castings
options.B: Defects in non-conducting materials such as rubber and timber
options.C: The chemical composition of an alloy
options.D: Surface and near-surface defects in electrically conductive materials

e: Eddy current testing is a non-destructive test that detects surface and near-surface defects in electrically conductive materials, from disturbances in the induced eddy currents; it cannot be applied to non-conductors.

q: In method study, the chart which records the sequence of operations, inspections, transportations, delays and storages occurring in a process, by means of a set of standard symbols, is known as the:

options.A: Flow process chart
options.B: String diagram
options.C: Multiple activity chart
options.D: SIMO chart

e: The flow process chart records the sequence of operations, inspections, transportations, delays and storages in a process by means of a set of standard symbols.

q: The lathe operation of 'parting off' means:

options.A: Producing a flat surface at the end of a workpiece
options.B: Cutting grooves on the workpiece
options.C: Cutting off the finished workpiece from the bar stock
options.D: Reducing the diameter of the workpiece over a part of its length

e: Parting off is the lathe operation of cutting off the finished workpiece from the bar stock; producing a flat end surface is facing, and cutting grooves is grooving.

q: 'Shot blasting' is carried out on castings and steel structures in a workshop in order to:

options.A: Harden their surface by heating and quenching
options.B: Clean and descale their surface and remove rust, e.g., before painting
options.C: Test them for internal defects
options.D: Coat them with a protective layer of zinc

e: Shot blasting is carried out to clean and descale the surface of castings and steel structures and to remove rust, e.g., before painting.

q: A distinctive feature of Gantt's task and bonus plan of wage payment is that:

options.A: The bonus of the worker is calculated as a proportion of the time saved
options.B: The worker is paid at two different piece rates according to his output
options.C: No time wage is guaranteed to the worker
options.D: A bonus is also paid to the foreman when the workers under him earn bonus by completing their tasks

e: A distinctive feature of Gantt's task and bonus plan is that a bonus is also paid to the foreman when the workers under him earn bonus by completing their tasks, which encourages the foreman to train and assist them.

q: A micrometer screw gauge, as used for precision measurement in a workshop, can ordinarily measure accurately up to:

options.A: 0.1 mm

e: A micrometer screw gauge, with its standard pitch and thimble divisions, can ordinarily measure accurately up to 0.01 mm.

q: Oxy-acetylene flame cutting of a steel plate in a workshop differs from gas welding in that, after the metal is heated to ignition temperature:

options.A: A filler rod is deposited in the joint
options.B: The flame is withdrawn and the metal is allowed to cool
options.C: A jet of pure oxygen is directed on to the heated metal, which burns the metal and blows away the oxide formed
options.D: A flux is applied to protect the surface

e: In oxy-acetylene flame cutting, after the metal is heated to ignition temperature, a jet of pure oxygen is directed on it, which burns the metal and blows away the oxide formed; this distinguishes cutting from welding.

q: A 'dry sand mould' in a workshop foundry is a sand mould which:

options.A: Is used in the moist condition, as rammed
options.B: Is dried or baked in an oven before the molten metal is poured into it, and is generally used for large castings
options.C: Is made without any moisture at all
options.D: Is made of metal instead of sand

e: A dry sand mould is a sand mould which is dried or baked in an oven before the molten metal is poured, and is generally used for large castings requiring greater strength and accuracy.

q: The failure of a machine component after a long period of service under repeated fluctuating (cyclic) stresses, at stress levels well below the ultimate tensile strength of the material, is known as:

options.A: Creep failure
options.B: Brittle fracture
options.C: Buckling
options.D: Fatigue failure

e: Failure after a long period of service under repeated fluctuating (cyclic) stresses, at levels well below the ultimate tensile strength, is known as fatigue failure.

q: Feeler gauges are used in a workshop for measuring:

options.A: Narrow gaps and clearances between two parts, such as the clearance between mating surfaces
options.B: The diameter of small holes
options.C: The pitch of screw threads
options.D: The thickness of large plates

e: Feeler gauges, being thin blades of known thickness, are used for measuring narrow gaps and clearances between two parts, such as mating surfaces.

q: In forging in the smithy of a workshop, the operation of 'upsetting' consists of:

options.A: Lengthening the workpiece by reducing its cross-section
options.B: Bending the workpiece to a required angle
options.C: Increasing the cross-section of the workpiece by shortening its length
options.D: Making a hole in the workpiece

e: In forging, upsetting consists of increasing the cross-section of the workpiece by shortening its length, as in forming the head of a bolt; lengthening by reducing cross-section is drawing out.

q: The Universal Account Number (UAN) allotted to a member of the Employees' Provident Fund:

options.A: Changes whenever the member changes his employer
options.B: Is allotted afresh on every transfer of the member
options.C: Is required only for members of the Employees' Pension Scheme
options.D: Remains the same throughout and is portable across employments, the member's provident fund accounts with different employers being linked to it

e: The Universal Account Number remains the same throughout and is portable across employments; the member's provident fund accounts with different employers are all linked to this single number.

q: The property of a material by virtue of which it can absorb energy and resist fracture under impact or shock loading is known as:

options.A: Toughness
options.B: Hardness
options.C: Stiffness
options.D: Elasticity

e: Toughness is the property by virtue of which a material can absorb energy and resist fracture under impact or shock loading; hardness, by contrast, is resistance to indentation.

q: Cutting fluids (coolants) applied during machining operations in a workshop serve principally to:

options.A: Harden the cutting edge of the tool
options.B: Increase the hardness of the workpiece
options.C: Prevent the formation of burrs on the workpiece
options.D: Cool the tool and the workpiece, lubricate the cutting zone and wash away the chips

e: Cutting fluids serve principally to cool the tool and the workpiece, lubricate the cutting zone and wash away the chips, thereby improving tool life and surface finish.

q: The property by virtue of which a metal can be hammered or rolled out into thin sheets without rupture is known as:

options.A: Ductility
options.B: Malleability
options.C: Brittleness
options.D: Tenacity

e: Malleability is the property by virtue of which a metal can be hammered or rolled out into thin sheets without rupture; being drawn into wires is ductility.

q: Workshop Manufacturing Suspense is called a 'suspense' head because:

options.A: Its balance is kept secret from audit
options.B: Expenditure is first collected on jobs without final allocation, the final head (Capital, Revenue or Stores) being determined on completion and transfer of the outturn
options.C: All expenditure booked under it is doubtful in nature
options.D: It is operated only at the close of the financial year

e: WMS is a suspense head because labour, material and on-cost are first collected on work orders under it, and the final head - Capital, Revenue or Stores - is decided only when the completed outturn is transferred out.

q: A shop draws a large quantity of material in advance for jobs which are yet to be taken in hand. The immediate effect of this is:

options.A: No effect on the balance under Workshop Manufacturing Suspense
options.B: An increase in the WMS balance without corresponding outturn, the material remaining charged to jobs not yet executed
options.C: A decrease in the WMS balance
options.D: An increase in Stores Suspense only

e: Material drawn in advance is debited to the jobs and so increases the WMS balance, even though no corresponding outturn has yet been produced or transferred out of the suspense.

q: Jobs in a shop are physically completed and completion reports have been received, but the transfer entries for the outturn are not passed for several months. This results in:

options.A: The WMS balance remaining inflated although the work has been completed
options.B: Automatic closure of the work orders concerned
options.C: Reduction of the WMS balance without any accounting entry
options.D: Transfer of the accumulated cost to shop on-cost

e: Outturn is cleared from WMS only by transfer entries on completion. If those entries are delayed, the accumulated cost stays in WMS and the balance remains inflated despite physical completion.

q: When manufactured articles are transferred from a workshop to the stores depot for stocking, the accounting link between the workshop and stores is effected by:

options.A: Debiting WMS and crediting the stores stock account
options.B: Debiting the Pension Fund and crediting WMS
options.C: Debiting shop on-cost and crediting the stores stock account
options.D: Crediting WMS under 'Issues to Stores' and debiting the stores stock account with the value of the articles

e: On transfer to stock, WMS is credited under Issues to Stores and the stores stock account is debited with the value of the manufactured articles, linking workshop and stores accounts.

q: The balance under Stores Suspense differs from the balance under Workshop Manufacturing Suspense in that Stores Suspense represents:

options.A: The value of jobs in progress in workshops
options.B: The value of stores stock held in depots, whereas WMS represents the value of jobs in progress in workshops
options.C: The unpaid wages of stores depot staff
options.D: The value of scrap awaiting disposal in depots

e: Stores Suspense represents the value of stores stock held in depots, while WMS represents the value of work in progress - labour, material and on-cost booked on unfinished workshop jobs.

q: In workshop accounts, the total debits booked to jobs during a period are termed 'outlay', while the total credits arising on transfer of completed work are termed:

options.A: Earnings
options.B: Receipts
options.C: Outturn
options.D: Appropriation

e: In workshop accounts, total debits booked to jobs in a period are called outlay, and total credits on transfer of completed work out of WMS are called outturn.

q: On-cost is distributed over jobs on the basis of direct labour charges mainly because:

options.A: Most indirect expenses of a shop are related to the labour employed and the time worked on jobs
options.B: The material cost of jobs cannot be ascertained in a workshop
options.C: Direct labour is the only cost incurred in a workshop
options.D: This basis is prescribed in the Stores Code

e: On-cost is absorbed on direct labour charges because most shop indirect expenses - supervision, idle time and the like - vary broadly with the labour employed and time worked on jobs.

q: Reconciliation of the Account Current between a workshop accounting unit and other accounting units is carried out in order to ensure that:

options.A: The cash balances of the two units agree with each other
options.B: All workers of the workshop have been paid correctly
options.C: The debits and credits advised by one unit have been accepted and accounted for by the other, and differences are cleared
options.D: The outturn programme of the workshop is achieved

e: Account Current reconciliation ensures that every debit and credit advised by one accounting unit has been accepted and accounted for by the other, and that differences are traced and cleared.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The shop on-cost percentage differs from shop to shop according to the indirect expenses of each shop.
2. General on-cost is applied at one uniform rate for the workshop as a whole.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both are correct: shop on-cost rates differ shop by shop with each shop's indirect expenses, while general on-cost, covering the workshop as a whole, is applied at one uniform rate.

q: The wages of a shop clerk who maintains the records of one particular shop only are treated in workshop costing as:

options.A: Direct labour of the jobs done in that shop
options.B: Indirect labour charged to the shop on-cost of that shop
options.C: Proforma on-cost of the workshop
options.D: General on-cost of the workshop

e: A clerk maintaining records of one shop only is indirect labour for that shop. His wages cannot be booked to any single job, so they are charged to that shop's on-cost.

q: The cost of the time office at the workshop gate, which records the attendance of staff of all the shops, is borne as:

options.A: General on-cost, since the time office serves the workshop as a whole
options.B: Shop on-cost of the erecting shop only
options.C: A direct charge on the first job taken up each day
options.D: Proforma on-cost of the workshop

e: The gate time office records attendance for all shops and serves the workshop as a whole, so its cost is a general charge borne as general on-cost, not any one shop's on-cost.

q: Which of the following charges forms part of proforma on-cost in workshop costing?

options.A: Power consumed by the machines of a shop
options.B: Wages of the foreman of a shop
options.C: Pension contribution in respect of workshop staff, charged notionally
options.D: Consumable stores used in a shop

e: Proforma on-cost covers notional charges not involving cash outgo in the workshop books, such as pension contribution for workshop staff, which is included to show the true full cost of outturn.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Under job costing, the cost of a job is ascertained on its completion.
2. Under process costing, the unit cost is ascertained for a period by dividing the process cost of the period by the output of the period.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both are correct: job costing ascertains the cost of a job on its completion, while process costing finds unit cost for a period by dividing the process cost of the period by its output.

q: The work order number is quoted on the job cards, material requisitions and completion report of a job primarily so that:

options.A: All labour, material and on-cost relating to the job can be linked and accumulated under that work order
options.B: The stores depot can fix the issue price of material
options.C: The pay of the workers on the job can be fixed
options.D: The job can be identified by the audit party

e: Quoting the work order number on job cards, material requisitions and completion reports links all labour, material and on-cost of the job so the total cost can be accumulated under that order.

q: Apart from classification by the head of account, work orders in a workshop are also broadly distinguished according to the nature of the work as:

options.A: Audited and unaudited work orders
options.B: Cash and credit work orders
options.C: Local and foreign work orders only
options.D: Manufacture work orders and repair work orders

e: Besides classification by head of account, work orders are broadly of two kinds by nature of work: manufacture work orders for making articles and repair work orders for repairs and overhaul.

q: The routine oiling and servicing of shop machinery, which is done month after month in the same manner, is charged in workshop accounts to:

options.A: A fresh specific work order issued every month
options.B: The same Revenue Standing Work Order allotted for such routine work
options.C: The Capital head of the workshop
options.D: Stores Suspense

e: Routine, repetitive work like oiling and servicing of shop machinery is charged to the same Revenue Standing Work Order allotted for it, not to a fresh specific order every month.

q: Manufacture of a special fixture required once only for a particular capital work should be executed under:

options.A: A Revenue Standing Work Order
options.B: A specific work order issued for that job
options.C: The on-cost standing work order of the shop
options.D: No work order at all

e: A one-time special fixture for a particular capital work is not routine work, so it must be executed under a specific work order issued for that job alone.

q: The route card of a job, besides showing the sequence of operations, serves during the execution of the job to:

options.A: Record the completion of each operation by the shop concerned as the job moves from shop to shop
options.B: Fix the wages payable to the workers on the job
options.C: Price the material issued to the job
options.D: Close the work order on completion of the job

e: The route card shows the sequence of operations and, as the job moves from shop to shop, each shop records completion of its operation on it, tracking progress of the job.

q: A route card differs from a job card in that the route card:

options.A: Records the attendance of the worker at the workshop gate
options.B: Is the document on the basis of which wages are paid
options.C: Prescribes the operations and the shops through which the job will pass, whereas the job card records the time spent by a worker on the job
options.D: Shows the material to be purchased for the job

e: The route card prescribes the operations and shops through which the job will pass, whereas the job card records the time actually spent by a worker on the job.

q: The time book of a workshop is compiled by the time keeper at the gate from:

options.A: The labour pay sheets of the workshop
options.B: The route cards of the jobs in progress
options.C: The stores issue notes of the depot
options.D: The gate attendance (clock) cards of the workers

e: The time book is compiled by the gate time keeper from the gate attendance or clock cards, which record each worker's time of arrival and departure.

q: An absentee statement prepared in a workshop from the gate and time records shows:

options.A: The machines which remained idle during the day
options.B: The workers absent or on leave during the period, so that their pay can be regulated in the pay sheets
options.C: The material not issued by the stores depot
options.D: The jobs remaining incomplete in the shop

e: The absentee statement, prepared from gate and time records, lists workers absent or on leave in the period so that their pay can be correctly regulated in the pay sheets.

q: The monthly Workshop Outturn Statement is compiled by the Workshop Accounts Office mainly from:

options.A: The completion reports and shop returns of outturn and expenditure
options.B: The stores price ledger maintained in the depot
options.C: The cash book of the workshop cash office
options.D: The muster rolls of casual labour

e: The monthly Workshop Outturn Statement is compiled by the Workshop Accounts Office from completion reports and shop returns showing outturn turned out and expenditure booked.

q: Agreement between Part I (quantity of outturn) and Part II (outlay) of the Workshop Outturn Statement is watched because a mismatch between the two indicates:

options.A: Excess staff posted in the shop
options.B: Wrong pricing of stores in the price ledger
options.C: Shortage of material in the stores depot
options.D: Jobs shown as completed but not transferred out, or expenditure booked on jobs not shown as completed

e: Agreement of Part I quantity of outturn with Part II outlay is watched because a mismatch shows jobs completed but not transferred out, or expenditure booked on jobs not shown as completed.

q: The Account Current rendered by a workshop accounts office is sent to the headquarters accounts office of the railway so that the workshop's transactions can be:

options.A: Incorporated in the general books of the railway, the workshop being a separate accounting unit
options.B: Audited directly by the C&AG
options.C: Published in the Works Programme (Pink Book)
options.D: Compared with the Traffic Book of the railway

e: The workshop is a separate accounting unit, so its Account Current goes to the headquarters accounts office for incorporation of its transactions in the general books of the railway.

q: In the Account Current of a workshop, work done by the workshop for other accounting units is shown as:

options.A: A credit in favour of those units
options.B: A debit against those units, and work done for the workshop by other units as a credit
options.C: A suspense item, without debit or credit
options.D: An item of shop on-cost of the workshop

e: In the Account Current, work done by the workshop for other accounting units is debited against those units, and work done for the workshop by other units is credited to them.

q: In the Workshop General Register, a separate folio or account is opened for:

options.A: Each worker employed in the workshop
options.B: Each machine installed in the workshop
options.C: Each stores item held in the depot
options.D: Each work order, showing the labour, material and on-cost booked on it and the outturn transferred

e: In the Workshop General Register a separate folio is opened for each work order, showing labour, material and on-cost booked on it and the outturn transferred against it.

q: Rolling stock provided under the Rolling Stock Programme is obtained by the railways by:

options.A: Purchase from passengers and the public
options.B: Transfer from the stores depot only
options.C: Manufacture in railway workshops and production units or purchase from trade, as decided for each item
options.D: Hire from other Government departments only

e: Rolling stock under the Rolling Stock Programme is obtained as decided for each item - manufactured in railway workshops and production units or purchased from trade.

q: The Machinery and Plant Programme differs from the Rolling Stock Programme in scope in that the M&P Programme covers plant and machinery required:

options.A: Only for locomotive workshops
options.B: Only for the Railway Board's office
options.C: Only for production units manufacturing locomotives
options.D: For workshops, sheds, depots and other units across the railway, and not merely for workshops alone

e: The Machinery and Plant Programme covers plant and machinery needed by workshops, sheds, depots and other units across the railway, not merely by workshops alone.

q: The itemised works sanctioned under the Rolling Stock Programme and the Machinery and Plant Programme are listed for the year in the railway's:

options.A: Traffic Book
options.B: Works Programme (Pink Book)
options.C: Stores Budget only
options.D: Appropriation Accounts

e: Itemised works sanctioned under the Rolling Stock and Machinery and Plant Programmes for the year are listed in the railway's Works Programme, commonly called the Pink Book.

q: Under the CLW pattern incentive scheme, a worker who saves time on a job is paid bonus for:

options.A: 50 per cent of the value of the time saved only
options.B: The full value of the time saved, his earnings being worked out on the allowed time for the job
options.C: 30 per cent of the value of the time saved only
options.D: The time taken by him only, with no bonus at all

e: Under the CLW pattern scheme, earnings are worked out on the allowed time for the job, so a worker who saves time gets the full value of the time saved as his incentive benefit.

q: A feature of the Group Incentive Scheme is that the bonus of every member of the group is affected by the outturn of the group as a whole, so that:

options.A: A shortfall in the outturn of the group reduces the incentive payable to all its members
options.B: Each member's bonus depends only on his individual output
options.C: The absence of a member has no effect on the group
options.D: Bonus is payable even if the group turns out no work

e: Under the Group Incentive Scheme bonus depends on the group's outturn as a whole, so a shortfall in group outturn reduces the incentive payable to every member of the group.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The individual (CLW pattern) incentive scheme suits work where the output of each worker can be measured separately.
2. The Group Incentive Scheme suits repair work where the outturn is the joint result of a group of workers.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both are correct: the individual CLW pattern suits work where each worker's output can be measured separately, and the group scheme suits repair work done jointly by a group.

q: A production unit works primarily to a production programme of new rolling stock, whereas a repair workshop works primarily to:

options.A: The same production programme of new rolling stock
options.B: The Machinery and Plant Programme of the railway
options.C: A programme of manufacture of stores items only
options.D: A Periodic Overhaul programme based on the arisings of stock due for overhaul

e: A production unit works to a production programme of new rolling stock, while a repair workshop works mainly to a Periodic Overhaul programme based on arisings of stock due for overhaul.

q: In a process shop where production flows continuously, valuation of work-in-progress at the end of a period becomes necessary because:

options.A: All jobs in a process shop are completed every day
options.B: Partly processed units remain in the process at the close of the period and their cost must be separated from the cost of the completed output
options.C: Process shops are not required to maintain cost records
options.D: The outturn of a process shop is transferred out only once a year

e: In a process shop, partly processed units remain in process at the close of a period, so work-in-progress must be valued to separate its cost from the cost of completed output.

q: Material used in the Periodic Overhaul of rolling stock belonging to another railway, carried out in a workshop, is not charged under PU 35 of the home railway because:

options.A: PU 35 covers labour charges and not material
options.B: Foreign rolling stock is overhauled free of cost
options.C: The material for such overhaul is supplied by the passengers
options.D: The cost of such overhaul is recoverable from the owning railway and is not a final charge on the home railway

e: Overhaul of another railway's stock is recoverable from the owning railway and is not a final charge on the home railway, so its material is not charged under PU 35 of the home railway.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The cost of a new component fitted during the Periodic Overhaul of a home railway coach forms part of the material cost of the overhaul.
2. A serviceable component released during the overhaul is credited to the overhaul job at its assessed value.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both are correct: a new component fitted during POH forms part of the material cost of the overhaul, and a serviceable released component is credited to the job at its assessed value.

q: Preventive maintenance can be built into the workshop programme in advance, whereas corrective maintenance cannot be so programmed, because corrective maintenance:

options.A: Is carried out only in production units
options.B: Requires no labour or material at all
options.C: Arises only on the failure or breakdown of the asset, which cannot be foreseen
options.D: Is always charged to Capital

e: Preventive maintenance is planned in advance, but corrective maintenance arises only on failure or breakdown of the asset, which cannot be foreseen, so it cannot be programmed beforehand.

q: A locomotive which has failed in service is sent to the workshop for emergent repair in order to put it back into service. This repair is an instance of:

options.A: Corrective maintenance
options.B: Preventive maintenance
options.C: Periodic Overhaul
options.D: Mid-Life Rehabilitation

e: Repair of a locomotive that has failed in service, to put it back into service, is corrective maintenance - it restores an asset after breakdown, unlike planned POH or preventive work.

q: If the Periodic Overhaul programme of a workshop is increased for a year, the linking of budgets requires that, besides the Workshop Manufacturing Suspense estimates, provision for the increased outturn to be transferred to revenue is also made in:

options.A: The Stores Suspense account
options.B: The respective Revenue Demand (working expenses) budget
options.C: The Pension Fund budget
options.D: The Contingency Fund

e: Increased POH outturn transferred to revenue must be matched by provision in the respective Revenue Demand working expenses budget, besides the WMS estimates, to link the budgets.

q: In production control in a workshop, 'routing' of a job means:

options.A: Determining the path of the job, i.e., the sequence of operations and the shops through which it will pass during manufacture
options.B: Paying the wages of the workers on the job
options.C: Inspecting the finished articles of the job
options.D: Preparing the labour pay sheets of the shop

e: Routing in production control means determining the path of a job - the sequence of operations and the shops through which it will pass during manufacture.

q: A combined workshop of Indian Railways is one which undertakes:

options.A: Only locomotive work
options.B: Only carriage and wagon work
options.C: Manufacture of stores items only
options.D: Work relating to more than one class of rolling stock, e.g., locomotives as well as carriages and wagons

e: A combined workshop undertakes work relating to more than one class of rolling stock, for example locomotives as well as carriages and wagons, under one workshop organisation.

q: The labour cost of a workshop job reaches the work order through the sequence:

options.A: Completion report, then gate card, then stores price ledger
options.B: Outturn statement, then absentee statement, then Plant Register
options.C: Job cards and tally sheets showing the time booked on the job, then the labour pay sheets distributing the wages over the jobs
options.D: Route card, then cash book, then Account Current

e: Labour cost reaches the work order through job cards and tally sheets showing time booked on the job, and then the labour pay sheets which distribute the wages over those jobs.

q: Where a repair job is executed in a workshop for the open line of its own railway, the completed outturn is transferred out of Workshop Manufacturing Suspense to:

options.A: The revenue head of the indenting department, while an article manufactured for stocking is transferred to Stores
options.B: Stores stock in all cases
options.C: The Capital head in all cases
options.D: The Pension Fund

e: Outturn of a repair job for the open line of the same railway is transferred from WMS to the revenue head of the indenting department, while an article made for stocking goes to Stores.

q: Work taken up in a workshop for an outside body on a deposit-work basis is executed:

options.A: Without any work order, as a casual job of the shop
options.B: By charging its cost directly to shop on-cost
options.C: Under a work order through Workshop Manufacturing Suspense like other jobs, the estimated cost together with departmental charges having been deposited in advance
options.D: Only after the close of the financial year

e: Deposit work for an outside body is executed under a work order through WMS like other jobs, after the estimated cost together with departmental charges has been deposited in advance.

q: The three elements of the cost of a workshop job are debited to its work order in the Workshop General Register from:

options.A: Labour from the gate cards, material from the gate passes and on-cost from the route cards
options.B: Labour from the muster rolls only, material from the cash book and on-cost from the Plant Register
options.C: Labour from the completion reports, material from the outturn statements and on-cost from the Account Current
options.D: Labour from the labour pay sheets, material from the stores issue summaries and on-cost from the on-cost statements

e: The three cost elements reach the work order folio from their source records: labour from labour pay sheets, material from stores issue summaries and on-cost from on-cost statements.

q: Labour has been booked on the tally sheets to a wrong work order, but the total wages paid to the worker are correct. The error in such a case affects:

options.A: Only the distribution of wages among jobs, and is corrected by a transfer entry between the work orders, without disturbing the amount paid to the worker
options.B: The amount payable to the worker, who must refund the wages
options.C: The balance under Stores Suspense only
options.D: The on-cost percentage of the workshop for the whole year

e: Booking correct wages to a wrong work order affects only distribution of cost among jobs. It is corrected by a transfer entry between work orders, without disturbing wages paid to the worker.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. An error in the rate of wages applied in a labour pay sheet affects the amount actually payable to the worker and calls for recovery or supplementary payment, as the case may be.
2. An error in booking correct wages to a wrong work order affects only the cost distribution among jobs and not the amount paid to the worker.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both are correct: a wrong wage rate affects the amount actually payable and needs recovery or supplementary payment, while a wrong work order affects only cost distribution among jobs.

q: Time booked by a worker on a job after the work order of that job has been closed and its outturn transferred is objectionable mainly because:

options.A: Closed work orders earn incentive bonus for the shop
options.B: It reduces the wages payable to the worker for that day
options.C: It increases the balance under Stores Suspense
options.D: It reopens a completed cost, distorts the transferred cost of the outturn and points to defective time booking in the shop

e: Time booked after a work order is closed reopens a completed cost, distorts the transferred cost of the outturn and shows defective time booking, so such booking is objectionable.

q: Material drawn from the stores depot for one job is diverted in the shop and actually used on another job. The correct accounting course is to:

options.A: Ignore the diversion, since both jobs belong to the same shop
options.B: Charge the material a second time to the second job, without crediting the first
options.C: Return the material physically to the depot in every case, even after consumption
options.D: Regularise the booking by a transfer between the two work orders, so that each job bears the material actually consumed on it

e: Material diverted from one job to another is regularised by a transfer between the two work orders, so that each job bears only the material actually consumed on it.

q: Idle time of workers in a shop arising because material requisitioned for the jobs in hand has not been received from the stores depot is, in costing terms:

options.A: A direct charge on the job which was waiting for the material
options.B: Normal idle time arising in the ordinary working of the shop, the wages for which are borne as on-cost
options.C: A charge to the Capital head of the workshop
options.D: Recoverable from the stores depot as a penalty in all cases

e: Wages for idle time caused by non-receipt of material in the ordinary course are normal idle time, a production overhead borne as on-cost, not a direct charge on the waiting job.
